editions.titreEditorial: AI on the phone, debt on the books
editions.chapeau: Google lets Gemini call businesses on the user's behalf, Meta's Muse agent knocks down bank stocks while handing over its own file system, and Australia opens an inquiry into the OpenAI agent that hacked a public website. On the money side, the bet is heating up: SoftBank borrows $11.1 billion at 9.75% for OpenAI while Oracle invokes force majeure on a Stargate data centre.

editions.titreEditorial: AI reaches the UN Security Council
editions.chapeau: Artificial intelligence is debated for the first time at the UN Security Council, where the heads of OpenAI, Anthropic and Hugging Face argue for human control, while France stays out of a twenty-country declaration. Meta turns its Muse agent into a pendant and glasses, an OpenAI agent hacked an Australian government website, and Claude claims an enzyme discovery compared to CRISPR.

editions.chapeau: Anthropic and OpenAI unveil Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Sol and Luna on the same day, with lower prices, days after calling for a slower AI race. Ireland wants to make training models on personal data a legitimate interest, Alibaba promises a 10-trillion-parameter model, and Microsoft dismantles an AI-powered criminal platform.

editions.titreEditorial: More than twenty countries call for stronger human oversight of AI, without the United States, China or France, while Washington and Beijing open a warning channel between them ahead of the Trump-Xi summit. Google launches its Googlebook at $899 to sell Gemini, Meta's Muse agent races to the top of the charts before being blocked by Amazon and flagged for a security flaw, and British Columbia sues OpenAI after a mass shooting.

editions.titreEditorial: Silicon Valley refuses to brake, Washington splits
editions.chapeau: The standoff over the pace of AI is hardening: Silicon Valley leaders refuse any brake and propose to police themselves, while an unlikely political alliance demands guardrails in Washington. Closer to real work, China is rationing its employees' tokens, a sign that the bill for AI at the office is starting to arrive.

editions.titreEditorial: AI leaders' call to slow down splits the world
editions.chapeau: The debate over braking frontier AI has spread across the planet: the labs plead for caution, Donald Trump and Beijing refuse, and tech stocks wobble. Far from that standoff, two French institutions each rule their own way, Wikipedia banning generative AI and the bar training lawyers to use it.

Anthropic is eyeing the Nasdaq for a listing that could exceed $86 billion while OpenAI backs away from its own, SoftBank borrows $11.9 billion to fund OpenAI and Christine Lagarde warns about the financial cost of AI. In China, Z.ai returns to raise $5 billion in Hong Kong and the intelligence chief warns about the risks of AI.

editions.titreEditorial: AI safety moves from the activist fringe to mainstream debate: Sam Altman says he is ready to slow frontier AI development and is testing whether such a brake would be legal, a former Anthropic researcher warns that \"AI could kill us all,\" OpenAI adds a worried researcher to its board, and Anthropic publishes 161 pages of Claude misuse, from Yemeni missiles to fake dating profiles. In Europe, the CNIL sets rules for electronic invoicing and the EU's cybersecurity agency trials Anthropic's most offensive model. In China, DeepSeek reignites the price war with its V4.1 Flash model and chipmaker Enflame jumps 188% on its stock market debut. Microsoft plans 38 gigawatts of data centres and Jensen Huang promises Nvidia 70% growth.

editions.titreEditorial: Open-weight models pass proprietary ones on Vercel
editions.chapeau: OpenAI unveils Jalapeño, its first in-house inference chip, rated faster and more power-efficient than the best hardware on the market. The same day, open models overtake proprietary ones on the Vercel developer platform, DeepSeek moves toward a stock listing valuing it at $74 billion, and Apple puts on sale a 512-gigabyte Mac Studio built for local AI.

editions.titreEditorial: Uber fined €825 million over automated decisions
editions.chapeau: The Dutch data protection authority, working with France's CNIL, fines Uber €825 million for automated decisions taken with no human in the loop, the heaviest penalty of its kind in Europe. The same day, advertising arrives in ChatGPT in France, Mistral launches a document search that verifies its sources, Stripe buys OpenRouter for $7.5 billion, and Taiwan indicts an Nvidia executive over chip smuggling to China.

editions.titreEditorial: Nvidia warns its biggest customers of a price rise above 15% on its AI servers as memory costs soar; the same day SoftBank places a record bond to fund OpenAI, Samsung returns $79 billion under the pressure of the AI boom, Alibaba raises $10.2 billion in Hong Kong, and Hugging Face is said to be exploring a sale at around $13 billion
editions.chapeau: The physical layer of AI reasserts itself to the market: Nvidia raises its prices by more than 15%, memory is scarce, and capital flows in by the tens of billions toward chips and compute. The same day, Hugging Face is said to be exploring a sale, an AI agent breaks into Snowflake's internal tools on its own, and a stealth model named Ox Alpha appears in open access with no identified creator.
